sentences.text: Researchers proposed an updated version of the Atkinson-Shiffrin memory framework to help organize the fragmented field of working memory research.
The model describes long-term storage as involving pattern-separated indexing in the hippocampus, while short-term memory relies on overlapping cortical codes for rapid comparison.
According to this framework, working memory depends on cue-dependent retrieval, and its capacity limits arise from interference between overlapping cortical representations.

The authors argue that background modeling processes like priors continuously influence perception, and that the distinction between storage types reflects neural coding differences rather than elapsed time.
